in_text_mentions: 38]. Moreover, as growth of fetal cardiac structures is dependent on the blood flow through them, persistent ventricular dysfunction can lead to secondary anatomic changes. Consequently, in a consecutive series of 150 recipient fetuses, 16% had a smaller than expected right ventricular outflow tract at the time of initial presentation [21]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real patient first-trimester ultrasound from a case of monochorionic triamniotic triplet pregnancy that developed twin-twin transfusion syndrome; the single gestational sac with three yolk sacs and intertwin membranes demonstrates the monochorionic placentation that is the anatomical substrate of TTTS (vocabulary finding monochorionic placentation, here triamniotic). B: 13 0/7-week ultrasound of the same monochorionic triplet pregnancy showing fetuses separated by intertwin membranes (arrow); demonstrates the monochorionic placentation underlying TTTS in this case report, though no frank TTTS fluid discordance is yet visible. C: 13 0/7-week ultrasound of the monochorionic triamniotic triplet pregnancy (caliper measurements) showing fetuses separated by intertwin membranes; documents the monochorionic placentation that predisposed this pregnancy to twin-twin transfusion syndrome.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Ultrasound image shows the recipient twin with marked polyhydramnios (DVP 13 cm), a classic manifestation of twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome. Caption and in-text evidence support the finding. b: Ultrasound image of the donor twin shows amniotic fluid at the lower limit of normal (DVP 4 cm), which contributes to the discordant amniotic fluid volumes in this borderline TTTS pregnancy. The donor finding is not classic oligohydramnios, so attribution relies on the paired discordance and the TTTS-focused article context.

in_text_mentions: edicine, University Hospital of Vienna, where a detailed ultrasonographic assessment revealed a viable cephalic fetus 1 with biometric measurements within normal range and a posterior placenta. The amniotic fluid was increased, with a deepest vertical pocket (DVP) of 13 cm, and the fetal bladder appeared distended (Figure 1). Doppler examination showed elevated resistance in the ductus venosus (pulsatility index for veins, PIV = 1.430) with a preserved a-wave, normal umbilical artery (UA) Doppler, and decreased MCA-PSV of 18.0 cm/s and a cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) of 0.661 (<1.0) (Figure 2).
